title: Token Trace Compass — role-aware cost filters, CSV-native export & pricing micro-patterns
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Context:
Redwood Console needs a compact, role-aware token-level cost exploration surface that supports rapid triage, ad-hoc attribution queries, and CSV-native exports for downstream chargeback workflows. Current token-level views are powerful but dense; customers ask for faster filters (by role, route, model variant), clearer amortization for multi-message conversations, and an export format that preserves attribution metadata for finance teams.

Goals:
- Create a prototype "Token Trace Compass" view that lets users slice token spend by role (system/user/assistant), model variant, route, and time window.
- Surface amortized per-message and per-embedding unit costs alongside absolute token cost.
- Provide an annotated CSV export that includes attribution columns (session_id, message_index, role, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, model, quant_profile, bucket_key) so customers can ingest into chargeback tools without losing lineage.
- Design pricing micro-patterns (compact rateband lens, delta-pricing overlay) to show how changes in batching/quantization would affect unit costs in-place.

Scope (this ticket):
- Low-fidelity -> high-fidelity prototype in Figma for Token Trace Compass list + detail pane.
- Two export modes: "Ledger CSV" (row-per-message) and "Rollup CSV" (row-per-session with amortized columns).
- Interaction patterns for role-based filters, quick-presets, and saved views.
- Handoff spec with annotated CSV schema, accessibility notes, and responsiveness guidelines.

Out of scope (future):
- Server-side export generation pipeline (ENG work).
- Deep SQL-backed ad-hoc query UI (will rely on existing analytics endpoints).

Proposed UX patterns & innovations:
- Compass header: breadcrumb + compact filters + a live cost-sparkline. Filters can be toggled by role chips (multi-select) and pinned to a saved view.
- Split list/detail: left column shows message-level rows with inline micro-metrics (token counts, cost, model). Right pane shows message trace with colored role bars and a cost waterfall for that message showing prompt/completion/kv-cache hits and amortized token share.
- Delta-pricing overlay: a panel control that lets a user simulate quantization or batching adjustments and see a per-token and per-session delta instantly (confidently powered by Optimize recommendations API).
- CSV-native export buttons with two preflight dialogs: (1) choose export mode + date range, (2) annotate columns and provenance (include policy for redaction of PII). Exports include a machine-friendly header block (JSON-encoded metadata line) followed by CSV rows.
- Pricing micro-patterns: small rateband pill that explains effective unit prices at current configuration with hover state to compare alternative packings.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototype with flows for: filtering by role, switching export modes, running a delta-pricing simulation, and saving a view.
- Annotated CSV schema and sample CSV (10 rows) attached to the ticket.
- Accessibility checklist completed (color contrast, keyboard nav, screen reader labels).
- Handoff doc with edge cases and engineering notes attached.

Success metrics:
- Design review sign-off from PM and Eng (list below).
- Usability test: time to find a per-message cost and export it reduced by 30% vs current console baseline (measured in next usability round).

Notes on trade-offs and constraints:
- Showing both amortized and absolute costs adds cognitive load; we prioritize compact visual encoding (inline sparklines + small numeric microcopy) and collapse advanced details into the right pane.
- CSV should be human-readable and machine-friendly — we propose a single-line JSON metadata header followed by a strict CSV schema to preserve provenance; some customers may prefer NDJSON but that adds backend effort.
- Simulations must be approximate (client-side) until Optimize API supports read-only simulation endpoints; label the numbers as estimates.

comments: 2026-02-22 | Jordan Alvarez: Initial sync — PM alignment on scope; agreed to prioritize CSV export and role-filtering over NDJSON export for Q1.

2026-02-27 | Liam O'Connor: Eng feasibility — server already emits message-level tokens but needs schema stabilization; ENG-EXPORT-789 opened. Backend prefers row-per-message ledger as canonical format.
2026-03-03 | Sofia Ramos: Research — quick guerrilla test with 6 customers shows strong preference for 'row-per-message' CSV for chargebacks; want a sample with session-level rollup as well.
2026-03-07 | Maya Patel: Design review notes — reduced visual weight of amortized numbers, added delta-pricing overlay mock, and added a compact rateband pill to the header.
2026-03-10 | Jordan Alvarez: PM feedback — add saved-views and a 'Share CSV link' pattern for finance teams. Confirmed privacy redaction flow for PII.
2026-03-12 | Liam O'Connor: Eng review — approves Figma interactions; flagged backend pagination requirement for large exports; added ENG-EXPORT-800 as follow-up for streaming CSV export.
2026-03-12 | Avery Chen: Closing notes — ready for high-fidelity and handoff; preparing annotated spec for engineers.
decisions: Use row-per-message CSV as primary export format (ledger) with optional session-rollup export.
Include a single-line JSON metadata header at top of CSV to preserve provenance.
Delta-pricing will be shown as client-side estimate until Optimize API simulation endpoint is available.
Prioritize role-aware filters (system/user/assistant) and model-variant chips in the first ship.
